title: Deepti Sharma Sets T20I Record as India Rout Thailand in Asia Cup Opener
excerpt: The veteran all-rounder claimed three wickets without conceding a run to become the leading wicket-taker in Women's T20 Internationals during India's dominant 94-run victory in Dubai.
body:
• Deepti Sharma reached 171 T20I wickets, surpassing Thailand's Thipatcha Putthawong to become the all-time leading wicket-taker in Women's T20 Internationals
  • Her spell of 3/0 in 1.1 overs was the most economical three-wicket haul by an Indian in Women's T20I history
  • Shafali Verma's explosive 64 off 36 balls anchored India's total of 159/9 before the bowlers restricted Thailand to 65
  • The milestone also marked Deepti's 150th T20I cap, making her the third Indian to reach the landmark

India launched their Women's T20 Asia Cup 2026 campaign with a commanding 94-run victory over Thailand at the Dubai International Stadium on Sunday, powered by a record-breaking bowling spell from Deepti Sharma that rewrote the history books of women's cricket.

Deepti, playing her landmark 150th T20I, returned figures of 3/0 in 1.1 overs — three wickets without conceding a single run — to finish the match with 171 career T20I wickets, surpassing Thailand captain Thipatcha Putthawong's mark of 170 to become the outright leading wicket-taker in Women's T20 Internationals.

A Record Spell for the Ages

The 29-year-old off-spinner's spell was clinical. After drawing level with Putthawong at 170 wickets by taking two wickets in the ninth over — reducing Thailand to 44/6 — Deepti returned in the 17th over and struck with her very first delivery to dismiss wicketkeeper Nannapat Koncharoenkai, who had top-scored for Thailand with 41.

Her figures of 3/0 became the most economical three-wicket haul by an Indian in Women's T20I history, surpassing Renuka Singh's previous best of 3/5 against Sri Lanka in Sylhet in 2022. Across all teams, there have been 26 instances of bowlers taking three or more wickets without conceding a run in Women's T20I cricket, but Deepti is the first Indian to achieve it.

"More than 150 wickets, it's a proud feeling to wear the Indian jersey with the Indian logo. It's about doing the right things as an Indian player."

— Deepti Sharma

Shafali Verma Lights Up the Top Order

Earlier, India's innings was anchored by opener Shafali Verma, who smashed a belligerent 64 off 36 balls, hitting eight fours and three sixes. The 22-year-old raced to her 19th T20I fifty off just 26 balls as India cruised past 100 in the 10th over.

Smriti Mandhana contributed a brisk 19 off 10 balls before a direct hit from Aphisara Suwanchonrathi ended her innings. Debutant Pratika Rawal, drafted in at No. 3 for the injured Jemimah Rodrigues, showed composure with 22 off 18 balls on her first T20I appearance.

However, India's innings unravelled dramatically after reaching 108/2. Thailand's leg-spinner Suleeporn Laomi triggered a collapse with figures of 3/26, while off-spinner Sunida Chaturongrattana claimed 2/31. India lost seven wickets for 29 runs before Kranti Gaud's unbeaten 15 off eight balls pushed the total to 159/9.

Bowlers Seal Dominant Victory

The target proved far beyond Thailand's reach. Seamers Nandani Sharma (3/18) and Kranti Gaud (1/26) removed both openers inside four overs, and left-arm spinner Shree Charani (2/10) kept the pressure on through the middle overs.

Thailand's innings never gained momentum outside of Koncharoenkai's lone resistance of 41. The team was bowled out for 65 in 16.1 overs, handing India a 94-run victory and a significant net run-rate boost in Group A.

What's Next

The seven-time Asia Cup champions next face Hong Kong on Thursday as they look to build on what was an emphatic start despite the batting hiccup. For Deepti, who also became the third Indian woman after Harmanpreet Kaur and Smriti Mandhana to play 150 T20Is, the tournament offers a stage to extend her newly claimed record. With 171 wickets, she leads the all-time list ahead of Putthawong (170), Rwanda's Henriette Ishimwe (164), England's Sophie Ecclestone (154), and Hong Kong's Kary Chan (153).
